subject: Post-call: latency bakeoff & p95/p99 acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Colin Mercer <colin.mercer@soteriahealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@soteriahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + perf goals — Soteria / Redwood follow-up

Thanks for the walkthrough today — helpful to see the hosted API and the streaming demo. A quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so we can finalize the internal SLO recommendation: 

1) Targets we care about (end-to-end, user request -> final token delivered):
   - p95: <= 250ms for short-form assistant queries (avg 32 tokens response)
   - p99: <= 450ms for same traffic profile
2) Concurrent workload: expected steady-state 120 QPS, spiky up to 420 QPS for 60-120s bursts during peak sessions.
3) Streaming: we require initial first-byte within 100ms for streaming-enabled flows, and subsequent token cadence consistent (no >200ms gaps) for the first 200 tokens.
4) Throughput / batching: our current provider uses batch size ~8 for cost efficiency; we need an option that maintains your latency SLOs without blowing cost 2–3x.

Action items from Soteria: we'll push traffic profiles and a 24h trace with real session distributions (attached sample_traffic_profile.csv).
Open question for Redwood: what’s the realistic latency envelope we should expect on hosted for our traffic (p95/p99) and what fallbacks look like when capacity gets constrained? Also curious for a short checklist of what you need from our side to run a bakeoff (live test vs replay).

If possible we'd like a 2-week window to validate (end of Aug). Happy to loop procurement if there are any contract/commit threshold considerations.

—Colin
Director of Product
Soteria Health

[attachment: sample_traffic_profile.csv (csv, 42KB)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Colin Mercer <colin.mercer@soteriahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency bakeoff & p95/p99 acceptance criteria

Thanks Colin — great notes and appreciate the traffic sample. High-level responses and next steps below; copying Jasmine (solutions eng) and Logan (performance lead) to lock in the bakeoff plan.

Quick answers:
- Hosted baseline: for short-form assistant queries (~32 token responses) on our hosted API we typically see p95 around 180–230ms and p99 380–430ms in the us-west region for single-request non-batched streaming. That’s a ballpark; exact numbers will depend on the exact model variant and tokenization.
- Bursts: our runtime supports fast autoscaling + thin-queued bursts; we'll need to validate tail behavior at your exact QPS spikes and session patterns. We expect sustained 120 QPS to be no problem; for 420 QPS bursts we'll propose an autoscaling runbook and an optional buffer pool (dedicated warm workers) to keep tail latency down.
- Streaming: we can achieve first-byte <100ms for typical cases; token cadence depends on model size and network path — Logan will show a token-interarrival sensitivity matrix.
- Cost/Batching tradeoff: we’ll produce recommendations on batching and quantization profiles that keep cost within ~1.2–1.7x of your incumbent while meeting SLOs (depends on model choice).

Proposed bakeoff plan (two-week window):
  1) Week 1: Replay test using your 24h trace (non-prod replay) + baseline hosted run. Redwood provides a replay harness and we run three repeat passes at representative concurrency (low, medium, spike).
  2) Week 2: Live streaming smoke test with synthetic spike generator + 4-hour continuous session run to observe prefix caching and KV cache effects.

What we need from you (prior to replay):
  - Full 24h trace in our replay schema (we can transform CSV)
  - A short set of 12 canonical prompts that represent short-form assistant usage (we’ll use these for streaming cadence checks)
  - Confirmation of the model family you want (small/medium/large) or we can propose 2 variants we think are closest to your incumbent.

Owner & timeline:
  - Logistics and replay harness: Jasmine (solutions eng) — will sync on ingest format and S3 link (action: Jasmine to schedule ingest call).
  - Performance run / token cadence matrix: Logan (performance) — will deliver matrix and initial p95/p99 expectations for the two model variants.
  - Contract/threshold questions: Alex — I’ll flag what commit levels we recommend for buffer pools if needed.

I’ll attach the call notes and a stub of the replay checklist. If end of August works we’ll aim to start week of Aug 23.

Next steps: Jasmine — can you take point on an ingest call with Colin? Logan — can you produce the token cadence sensitivity doc by EOD Thu? I’ll schedule a 30m kickoff with Soteria for Wed.

Best,
Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment: soteria-call-notes.pdf (pdf, 18KB)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Colin Mercer <colin.mercer@soteriahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency bakeoff & p95/p99 acceptance criteria

Thanks — Colin & Priya, happy to take the ingest and run coordination. Quick operational notes and the checklist I’ll use on the ingest call: 

Ingest checklist (what I’ll ask for on the call):
  - S3 access or a signed link to the 24h trace (ideally parquet, else CSV)
  - Mapping doc for fields (timestamp, session_id, prompt, response_len, user-agent)
  - Any redaction rules (PII or PHI) — we will mirror your redaction if required; we also support on-the-fly hashing for IDs
  - Canonical prompt list (12) + expected short/long label per prompt
  - Preferred model variants (or say “recommend”)
  - Target test windows (we propose Aug 23–28 for replay, Aug 30–Sep 3 for live smoke)

Operational assumptions we’ll validate during the replay:
  - Replay is client-side timed to emulate arrival distributions; we’ll run at 100%, 40%, and 150% of the trace concurrency to measure sensitivity.
  - For p95/p99 computation we’ll compute end-to-end request -> final-token time (streaming measured as first-byte and end-to-end completion).
  - We’ll surface a small dashboard with per-route p95/p99 and a tail heatmap for queuing spikes.

Deliverables after bakeoff:
  - Replay report: p50/p95/p99 for each test pass + recommended model variant and batching profile.
  - Token cadence matrix (Logan) and suggested streaming buffer config.
  - Cost estimate: per-1M tokens for proposed profile vs incumbent.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute ingest call for Thu Aug 12 at 10:00 PT — Colin, can you confirm that time or suggest alternatives?

—Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
